chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who hastened to give the zakat of his wealth, then the recipient became affluent before the end of the year, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The giver must repeat the zakat.'

key_terms.رَأْسِ السَّنَةِ: The end of the lunar year (hawl)

ai.seo_question: What happens to zakat if the recipient becomes rich before the year ends?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 're-distribution' (i'adah) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the integrity of zakat funds by verifying the recipient's eligibility at the time of actual receipt. It underscores the scholarly view that zakat is not merely a fixed obligation upon payment but a conditional transfer dependent on the recipient's ongoing status of need (faqir) or poverty. This prevents the misallocation of sacred wealth to those who have already achieved financial stability, aligning with the broader objective of purifying the giver's wealth effectively.
